A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CSBM-based study of graph attention, despite the changed title and formatting. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–L are available and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original synthetic experiments and evaluations on Citeseer, Cora, and Pubmed. Appendix L adds classification comparisons and measured runtimes.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendix L retain the original synthetic and real-world experimental results, including classification curves and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: The sign-based attention rule, softmax aggregation, and hybrid GCN/GAT construction remain unchanged. Separating the classification output as Xout = sgn(XL) in v2 Equation 1 is an equivalent notational rewrite of v1 Equation 4.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic CSBMs and Citeseer, Cora, and Pubmed datasets. The noise scenarios and Appendix L's one-versus-all classification task are retained.

E2.justification: Section 4 retains the GCN, GAT, and GAT* comparisons. Appendix L still compares GCN, GAT-jmlr from Fountoulakis et al. (2023), and GAT*. Removing the main-text pointer to Appendix L does not remove that comparison.

E3.justification: The experimental settings remain unchanged, including synthetic n = 3000 and sigma = 10, network depths, attention-intensity schedules, evaluation metrics, default PyTorch Geometric splits, and Appendix L's feature adjustment procedure.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the attention-intensity and noise sweeps, the 100-layer over-smoothing experiment, the hybrid-network comparison across SNRs, and real-world feature-noise robustness analyses. No analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: The synthetic results remain averaged over 100 trials, and Appendix L retains its single-run runtime measurement procedure. Existing plotted bands are unchanged; no new seed information, uncertainty estimation, or significance testing is reported.

E6.justification: All ten plot panels in Figures 1–3 retain identical image content and findings. Table 3 still reports 8.63, 10.03, and 8.93 seconds for GCN, GAT-jmlr, and GAT*, respectively. No result entries or numerical values change.

T1.justification: The assumptions, four main theorems, corollary, lemmas, and appendix derivations retain their mathematical substance, including the perfect-classification SNR threshold. Equation renumbering and separating output notation do not introduce new theory or proof steps.

C1.justification: The abstract and main contributions retain the same claims about noise-dependent attention benefits, high-SNR over-smoothing mitigation, and multi-layer perfect classification. The new title and Impact Statement emphasize claims already present in v1.

C2.justification: The conclusion replaces v1's future-work list with explicit limitations concerning omitted learnable parameters, single-head attention, and dependencies from attention across layers. Its final-layer-only characterization fits Appendix J's construction but is not clearly reconciled with the retained multilayer-attention analysis in Section 3.3.

D1.justification: Hardware specifications, dataset characteristics, splits, feature-processing instructions, and Appendix L's parameters remain unchanged. Both versions report beta = 0.2 and R = 1 for GAT-jmlr, t = 1 for GAT*, and 100 epochs for runtime measurement.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning against prior graph-attention and over-smoothing research remain unchanged. Added citation years and expanded publication metadata concern existing references rather than newly cited research.

P1.justification: The title changes, the conclusion is partly rewritten, and an Impact Statement is added. Section 2.2 shortens explanations and moves the GAT-layer clarification into a footnote. Most prose and the section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from a single-column preprint layout to a two-column conference layout. Figure 1 changes from four panels in one row to a 2-by-2 arrangement, and Figure 2 becomes a two-row arrangement. Appendix displays, typography, and headers are also reformatted, while their content is retained.

improvement.justification: The new limitations paragraph usefully explains restrictions beyond v1's future-work list, but its final-layer-only statement creates ambiguity alongside Section 3.3 and Appendix I. The new output notation is also not propagated into Definition 1. With unchanged proofs and experimental evidence, these limited benefits and clarity problems do not establish a reliable net direction in overall quality.
